screen33-a1.glyph: dimmed grey strip along the right screen edge, no symbol of its own
screen33-a1.description: dimmed grey strip along the right edge beside the open side panel; the ghost glyph of the screen beneath shows through it
screen33-a1.visible_text: none; the only mark inside it is the dimmed ghost glyph belonging to the covered screen
screen33-a1.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Close navigation menu" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen33-a1.convention_relied_on: tapping the dimmed area outside a side panel to close it is an Android convention, but the strip shows another control's glyph as its only face — my reading, confidence medium
screen33-a1.initial_rationale: the strip has no face of its own; what a user sees inside it is the ghost glyph, which suggests the strip does that glyph's job
screen33-a1.deciding_evidence: same control as screen2-a1 (identical appearance, words and position in the same repeated state); tested once there and the verdict carried: the only visible thing in the strip is a glyph from the covered screen, and tapping it closes the panel instead of doing that glyph's job
screen33-a1.recommendation: dim the covered screen enough that its controls do not read as live, or give the panel its own visible close control (an X or 'Close') at the top

screen33-a2.description: large word 'Claude' at the top of the side panel
screen33-a2.visible_text: "Claude" (the product's name, set as a title)
screen33-a2.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Claude" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen33-a2.initial_rationale: the visible text is the product's name; it reads as a title, not an action, and says nothing about what pressing it does
screen33-a2.deciding_evidence: same control as screen2-a2 (identical appearance, words and position in the same repeated state); tested once there and the verdict carried: the title is actionable and starts a new chat, which the product name gives no hint of
screen33-a2.recommendation: make the title non-interactive, or label the action it performs (e.g. 'Home' / 'New chat')

screen33-a3.deciding_evidence: same control as screen2-a3 (identical appearance, words and position in the same repeated state); tested once there and the verdict carried: opened the Chats list it names

screen33-a4.description: 'Projects' row with a stacked-tray glyph in the side panel
screen33-a4.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Projects" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict

screen33-a5.description: 'Code' row with a </> glyph in the side panel
screen33-a5.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Code" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen33-a5.initial_rationale: 'Code' alone does not say whether this writes code, shows code, or opens a coding tool; a first-time user cannot tell what they get
screen33-a5.deciding_evidence: same control as screen2-a5 (identical appearance, words and position in the same repeated state); tested once there and the verdict carried: the row leads to a paid-product upgrade page; neither the product nor the paywall is conveyed by the single word 'Code'
screen33-a5.recommendation: name the destination, e.g. 'Claude Code (coding assistant) — Pro'

screen33-a6.description: 'Artifacts' row with a shapes glyph in the side panel
screen33-a6.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Artifacts" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen33-a6.initial_rationale: 'Artifacts' is product jargon; a first-time user does not know what an artifact is
screen33-a6.deciding_evidence: same control as screen2-a6 (identical appearance, words and position in the same repeated state); tested once there and the verdict carried: neither the row nor the screen it opens explains the term
screen33-a6.recommendation: rename or caption it in plain words, e.g. 'Artifacts — documents, code and designs Claude made for you'
